newsitem.title: UK: Pearson at 3-month high, ABN AMRO upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Pearson at 3-month high, ABN AMRO upgrades.

text.p: Shares in British media and leisure company Pearson Plc soared to a three-month high on Tuesday as broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett upgraded its recommendation to 'buy' from 'hold'.

Pearson shares were 48p higher to 740.5p by 1350 GMT, extending Monday's 26.5p gain. They have now gained more than 11 percent since the company announced higher-than- expected first-half results on Monday.

An ABN AMRO analyst said the upgrade was based largely on the belief the stock market performance should improve following evidence that the company's new management was taking action to exploit the company's assets.
The company has a stellar portfolio of assets, including the Financial Times newspaper and Penguin books, but its management has long stood accused of under-exploiting these brands.
"The opportunities are virtually endless. They can do a lot more on both the revenue side and the cost side," said the ABN AMRO analyst.

Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino, who has been in the job little more than six months, vowed on Monday to deliver annual earnings growth of in excess of 10 percent and double the value of the company within five years.
